tweet.text:
This is f*cking insane.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was asked what skills people should focus on as AI starts taking over more workplace tasks.

His message is becoming harder to ignore:

AI isn't just a productivity tool anymore.

It's learning to do the actual work.

Writing code, analyzing financial reports, building presentations, researching markets, handling customer support, and managing entire workflows.

And the scary part?

It's getting better every month.

Think about what this means for someone starting their career in 2026.

A company that once needed 5 junior employees might soon need just 1 person managing AI agents.

The question is no longer whether AI will change your career.

It's whether you'll know how to work with it.

If I were starting my career from scratch in 2026, I'd learn these 14 free resources:

1. Learn the foundations

→ Google AI Essentials: https://t.co/aCaRs4T3dc

→ Microsoft Generative AI for Beginners:
https://t.co/WKeWqNznw0

→ Elements of AI: https://t.co/pSYGpvMGK3

2. Master prompting

→ OpenAI Prompt Engineering Guide:
https://t.co/maqJL6BjMG

→ DAIR AI Prompt Engineering Guide:
https://t.co/bBqcLJyMwR

→ Anthropic Prompt Engineering Tutorial:
https://t.co/rTFQEgm3Sp

3. Learn to build AI agents

→ Hugging Face Agents Course:
https://t.co/XxVJXVsC1t

→ Microsoft AI Agents for Beginners:
https://t.co/dzuxf0wUtd

→ CrewAI: https://t.co/2KX6bJ3bEr

→ LangChain: https://t.co/XeuOPEjmzD

4. Understand how AI actually works

→ Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks Zero to Hero:
https://t.co/OuVgCfHcDV

→ Google's Machine Learning Crash Course:
https://t.co/uScGQznAX5

5. Build real-world projects

→ Awesome LLM Apps:
https://t.co/59h2VAtW0F

→ Anthropic Cookbook:
https://t.co/xnaZrtj5M5

Total cost: $0.

But here's what most people will get wrong:

They'll spend the next year collecting AI tools, watching tutorials, and saving resources.

Very few will actually build something.

Don't just learn how to prompt AI.

Learn how to:
• Break complex problems into smaller tasks.
• Build workflows that save hours.
• Connect different AI tools.
• Create and manage AI agents.
• Verify AI-generated results.
• Use AI to solve real business problems.

The future won't belong only to people who know how to use AI.

It will belong to people who know how to turn AI into results.

Don't spend 2026 watching the AI revolution happen. Learn how to build with it.

Save this and send it to someone starting their career.

tweet.text:
今天 GitHub 被「浏览器三巨头 + 安全扫描 + 代码审查」大厂联军屠榜了！

5 个星标暴增最狠的项目，专业拆解下！

1. GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src

Modern Web Guidance 的源码仓：把 Web 平台最佳实践和浏览器兼容数据做成技能，直接塞进你的编程 Agent，让它别再写过时套路；一行 npx 就能安装、搜索指南、扫描旧代码。由 Chrome、Edge、Firefox 和 MDN 团队共同维护。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/jfCyveI5ad

AI 写前端最大的毛病就是「十年前的 Stack Overflow 味」，这回浏览器厂商亲自下场补课。1,875 星一天，含金量拉满！

🟢

2. openai/codex-security

OpenAI 官方的 Codex Security 命令行和 TypeScript SDK：扫描仓库或 Git 改动、验证漏洞、生成补丁并复核修复，还能导出 SARIF/JSON/CSV，接 Linear、Jira、GitHub 和 CI。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/L47ZkoALHP

找漏洞、验漏洞、修漏洞一条龙，安全工程师多了个不下班的搭档。754 星一天，总星 1.3 万+，AppSec 正式进入 Agent 时代！

🟢🟢

3. tailscale/tailcat

Tailscale 官方的「不用 Tailscale 的 Tailscale」：像 netcat 一样在两台机器间开 WireGuard 端到端加密隧道，自动打洞直连，不需要账号、不需要 root，纯用户态命令行和 Go 库。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/IAzTAftQrk

一个短地址就能把两台机器连起来，穿透 NAT 像喝水一样简单。324 星一天，网络老炮狂喜！

🟢🟢🟢

4. alibaba/open-code-review

阿里内部用了两年的 AI 代码审查工具开源：读 Git diff，交给带工具调用的 Agent 去翻全文件、搜代码库，输出精确到行的结构化评审意见；README 称同模型下精确率和 F1 明显高于通用 Agent，token 只用约九分之一。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/52v05wxt3p

数万开发者、数百万缺陷练出来的审查官，现在人人能请。206 星一天，总星 5 万+，大厂内功直接外放！

🟢🟢🟢🟢

5. ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp

Chrome DevTools 官方给 Agent 的接口：MCP 服务 + 命令行，让 Claude、Cursor、Copilot 等编程 Agent 直接操控、检查一个真实 Chrome，录性能 trace、看网络请求、截图、读控制台。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/nyjMQvI3Vh

Agent 终于不再「盲写前端」，能自己打开 F12 找 bug 了。145 星一天，总星 5.5 万+，浏览器调试彻底交给 AI！

🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢

⚠️⚠️
总结：
今天的榜单写满了一个信号：大厂开始把自家内功直接喂给 Agent（Chrome 的 Web 指南和 DevTools、OpenAI 的安全扫描、阿里的代码审查）。工具越来越像「给 AI 用的」，谁先把 Agent 武装到牙齿，谁就站在下一波生产力的 C 位。

repos.name: shitianfang/jev-use
repos.description: Claude Code / Codex / pi plugin that hands agent steps needing no text output to Jev (TypeSafe's judgment model) — measured p50 ~230 ms and ~$0.02 per 1,000 judgments, with typed escalation back to the LLM

tweet.text:
Jev 应用分享又燃爆了 🔥

shitianfang 的 LLM + Jev 双人搭档、andududu 的 Jev 调用实况地图、tostechbr 的「话没说完就动手」语音控制、bytelabs-oss 的皇室战争机器人、AgriciDaniel 的技能分诊台……全网玩家把 Jev 玩成了下一代「快手搭档 + 调用监视器 + 读心语音助手 + 电竞选手 + 智能分诊员」:

1️⃣ shitianfang/jev-use（https://t.co/EQsfmfRyzt）

给 Claude Code、Codex 和 Pi 用的插件：不需要输出文字、只要快速判断的步骤交给 Jev，需要写内容时再交回大模型；作者实测拦截危险命令约 230 毫秒、不耗大模型 token，200 条消息 7 次调用完成上下文压缩；一行 npx 安装；72 星。
“写字交给大模型，拍板交给 Jev”！

2️⃣ andududu/jeview（https://t.co/NXaIU936hX）

一个非官方的本地 Jev 可视化网关：把 Jev 客户端指向它，它带着你的 key 转发请求，把每次调用存进本地 SQLite，并实时画在一张地图上；只需 Node 24，零依赖；作者声明与 TypeSafe 无关联；68 星。
“每一次 Jev 判断，都看得见”！

3️⃣ tostechbr/partway（https://t.co/wONjCwwhGk）

macOS 语音控制：你说的每个词都拿去问 Jev，约 200 毫秒返回带概率的判断，所以一句话还没说完，备忘录就已经打开了；能开应用、新建笔记、开网站、搜索、打字，还能一口气连说多个指令；32 星。
“你还在说，它已经做完了”！

4️⃣ bytelabs-oss/clash-jev（https://t.co/xiUfLvhBWV）

用 Jev 在真实安卓手机上打《皇室战争》：OpenCV 把实时画面读成 JSON 局面，Jev 每次约 135 毫秒依次选策略、选卡、选落点，程序确认能下再点击；不用强化学习、不用模拟器，没有训练过任何出牌策略；37 星。
“没练过一局，照样上场对线”！

5️⃣ AgriciDaniel/gatekeeper（https://t.co/B6RJkcTj9J）

在你的 AI 选工具之前，先决定这条请求该交给哪个 Agent 或技能：代码先过规则，剩下的语义问题交给 Jev 做带概率的选择，再按置信度给出放行、转交、建议、需确认、升级或拦截；每次不到一美分、约半秒；目前以 Claude Code 钩子安装；25 星。
“请求进门先分诊，别让 AI 瞎猜”！

repos.name: patchy631/time-to-first-token
repos.description: A 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day roadmap for LLM inference serving and optimization. vLLM, SGLang, quantization, speculative decoding, benchmarking.

tweet.text:
GPU architecture, clearly explained.

The usual assumption is that a faster GPU means more compute, so a chip rated for more operations per second should generate more tokens per second.

That rarely holds. You can rent a top-end chip, load a model, watch utilization sit high, and still get a few dozen tokens per second out of hardware capable of a thousand trillion operations.

The arithmetic units are not the limit. They spend most of their time waiting for numbers to arrive.

Memory bandwidth is how fast those numbers can be delivered, and it grows far more slowly than arithmetic capability with each new generation.

The H100 makes this concrete. It does 989 trillion operations per second at 16-bit precision, while its memory delivers 3.35 trillion bytes per second.

Divide one by the other and you get about 295. That is how many operations the chip has to perform on every byte it fetches just to keep its arithmetic units busy.

Generating a token comes nowhere close. Each weight gets multiplied by one number and added into a running total, so two operations per weight, and each weight costs 2 bytes to read at 16-bit precision.

That works out to 1 operation per byte, roughly three hundred times short of what the chip needs.

Once you see that, the layout of a GPU stops looking arbitrary. All of it is organized around distance, because every trip to fetch a value is the expensive part.

Execution is nested in four steps, smallest first.

→ Thread. The smallest unit of work, doing arithmetic on its own handful of values.

→ Warp. A group of 32 threads that move in lockstep and share a single instruction, which is what the hardware actually schedules.

→ Thread block. A batch of warps, up to 32 of them or 1024 threads, handed to one compute unit and staying there until it finishes.

→ SM. The streaming multiprocessor, a small self-contained machine with its own arithmetic units, its own storage, and its own scheduler. An H100 has up to 132 of them.

Memory is nested along the same lines, and that is the part that decides your speed.

→ Registers. 256 KB per SM, split so each thread gets a private slice nobody else can read. A value here already sits next to the thing that needs it, so reading it costs nothing worth measuring.

→ Shared memory and L1. A few hundred KB per SM. Shared memory is the only level you place things into yourself, and every thread in a block can read it, which is where the name comes from.

→ L2 cache. Around 50 MB sitting below all the SMs, and the first level every one of them can see. Reaching it means leaving your own SM.

→ HBM (High Bandwidth Memory). Around 80 GB, holding model weights, the KV cache, and activations. It sits outside the processing chip entirely, and reaching it is the slowest thing a GPU does.

The nesting is what buys you speed. Anything that stays inside one SM is fast because nobody outside needs to see it, and anything the whole chip has to agree on pays for the trip down.

Add up the registers across every SM and you get roughly as much storage as the L2 underneath them, which is nothing like the neat pyramid you see on a CPU.

So making a GPU faster is mostly about how many round trips to HBM you can avoid. FlashAttention is the clearest case, since ordinary attention writes a large intermediate result all the way down and reads it back, while the tiled version keeps it up on the SM and runs far faster doing the same arithmetic.

I wrote the full breakdown of how a GPU works, from this layout up to the ratio that sets your token rate. The article is quoted below.

I have also put together a 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day roadmap for engineers who want to actually run LLM inference in production, not just read about it.

Check this out: https://t.co/pOqkWvDJ2d

(don't forget to star 🌟)

Stay tuned for more on this! https://t.co/LZBmYCeFnK

repos.name: karpathy/micrograd
repos.description: A tiny scalar-valued autograd engine and a neural net library on top of it with PyTorch-like API

tweet.text:
a 19-year-old from China built a swarm of Claude Code agents that researches, writes, and verifies outputs automatically.

meanwhile, Andrej Karpathy has 7 free GitHub repositories that take you from understanding a single neuron to building AI agents that run experiments overnight.

these repositories have attracted over 300K GitHub stars combined.

you can learn how neural networks work, understand tokenization, train your own GPT, explore raw C/CUDA, and build systems that let AI agents experiment and improve models.

and you don’t need to spend $200 on another AI course to get started.

here’s the learning path, in the right order:

1. micrograd : understand how neural networks learn

learn the fundamentals of automatic differentiation and backpropagation.

it’s a tiny neural network library built in Python that helps you understand what’s happening behind the scenes.

https://t.co/Iht0Cetjlc

2. nn-zero-to-hero : learn neural networks from scratch

a free video course that takes you from a single neuron to building a GPT.

you get explanations, code, and practical exercises along the way.

https://t.co/FeWEJxkp5C

3. minbpe : understand how AI reads text

before an LLM can process text, it needs to turn it into tokens.

this repository teaches you how Byte Pair Encoding works and how tokenizers are built.

https://t.co/sXEidpgupi

4. nanoGPT : build your own GPT

learn how GPT models are trained and fine-tuned.

you’ll explore the actual training process instead of treating language models like black boxes.

https://t.co/dEVv0vaSDI

5. llm.c : understand the raw machinery

go deeper into language model training with C and CUDA.

this strips away much of the framework abstraction and lets you see how the underlying training operations work.

https://t.co/R85TMYg7og

6. nanochat : build a complete ChatGPT-style system

this brings together tokenization, model training, evaluation, and inference into one project.

it’s a practical look at how a complete conversational AI system comes together.

https://t.co/bQzLQcds6o

7. autoresearch : let AI agents run experiments

this is where the journey gets really interesting.

AI agents modify training code, run experiments, evaluate results, and keep improvements that work.

instead of manually testing every idea, you build a system that can conduct research experiments automatically.

https://t.co/arb8FTNMqe

here’s the order i’d follow:

→ start with micrograd to understand the fundamentals.

→ use nn-zero-to-hero to build your knowledge.

→ learn tokenization with minbpe.

→ move into GPT training with nanoGPT.

→ explore the lower-level implementation in llm.c.

→ study the complete workflow in nanochat.

→ finish with autoresearch and autonomous AI experimentation.

why should you save this?

because these repositories give you a practical learning path through the technology powering modern AI, from the mathematics behind neural networks to agents that can run experiments on their own.

don’t just learn how to prompt AI.

learn how the technology actually works.

bookmark these repositories and follow me for more free resources, tools, and AI workflows that can help you become a better builder. https://t.co/VySBto3XA6

它还把「忠实度」拆成 7 个可以量化的指标，README 里写一本 273 页的中文书跑下来，覆盖率是 1.00。

版权这块也做得很克制：单条引文不超过 150 字，总引文比例不超过 3%，用别人的书生成的 Skill 默认私有，想公开分发得额外加两道确认参数。

读完一本书不难，难的是让 AI 也照着它做事。

OpenFilm 是一个开源的 AI 视频 Agent，让 Codex、Claude Code 这类编码 Agent 来做视频，片子里的每个镜头其实都是一个网页。

跟它说一句「给我的命令行工具做一条 20 秒的发布视频，配上音乐」，它就开始写，本地的编辑器会在浏览器里显示片子一点点成形。

支持 macOS、Windows、Linux 系统，另外有 macOS 和 Windows 的桌面版，装好就能用。官方那条 1 分 42 秒的发布视频，就是用它从头做到尾的。

repos.name: NVIDIA/Personal-AI-Router
repos.description: Router that virtually distributes inference across connected devices in the home.

tweet.text:
Nvidia built a tool that lets multiple pcs share their local AI workloads. 

this free open-source project connects multiple computers on the same network and distributes AI inference requests between them.

it’s called NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR).

and it already has 1.8K+ GitHub stars.

here’s what makes it interesting:

→ share local AI workloads: connect multiple computers and route independent AI requests to whichever machine can handle them.

→ automatic request routing: PAIR considers model availability, supported inference engines, and current workload when choosing a machine.

→ mix different operating systems: connect Windows, macOS, and Linux computers in the same network.

→ multiple inference engines: supports Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and vLLM, with platform and hardware requirements.

→ API compatibility: exposes Ollama-compatible, OpenAI-compatible, and Anthropic Messages API endpoints, so compatible apps and agents can connect to your local models.

→ multi-agent workflows: distribute concurrent requests from applications running multiple AI agents across your connected machines.

→ live monitoring: track connected devices, jobs, GPU usage, and memory usage.

→ local processing: when your clients, models, engines, and machines are all local, prompts and responses stay on your local network.

here’s how to set it up:

1. download NVIDIA PAIR from the GitHub Releases page.
2. install it on each computer you want to connect.
3. open PAIR and install or start an inference engine such as Ollama or LM Studio.
4. download a model on each machine.
5. go to Settings → Cluster and pair your computers using the six-digit PIN.
6. connect your AI applications using the API endpoint provided by PAIR.

that’s it. your connected computers can now share incoming inference requests.

a few important things to know:

→ it doesn’t combine multiple GPUs into one giant GPU or split a single model across computers. each request is handled by one machine.

→ each computer still needs enough memory and compatible hardware to run its selected model.

→ you can use the desktop application or a terminal interface for machines without a graphical desktop.

→ it supports Windows 11, Linux, and macOS, with x64 and ARM64 builds. Windows on ARM is experimental.

→ it’s free and open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

if you have multiple computers and want to build a local AI setup, this is definitely worth exploring.

save this, and follow for more useful open-source tools. Anthropic's agent team beat a single agent by 90%. Cursor's built a browser in a week. Other big labs are moving the same way.

This is how they work, and how you can run one today. https://t.co/ZryIeBcIFa

Swiplet 是用 SwiftUI 写、直接跑在 Swipt 里的小应用，自动化流程也能做成一个个独立的小程序。

手机以前要用手指点，现在可以交给 agent 点了。

repos.description: Open-source, self-hosted Slack alternative where your team and AI agents work together in channels and DMs. Agents run on Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini or Grok, with MCP tools, their own computer and browser, routines, memory and approvals. tweet.text:
团队里用上了 Agent，可它们各待在各的窗口里，谁让它干了什么、干到哪一步，别的同事基本看不到，交接全靠截图转述。

https://t.co/pFzUO9u0EA 是一个开源、可以自己部署的团队聊天工具，定位是 Slack 的替代品，特别的地方是 Agent 和人待在同一个频道里。

每个 Agent 有自己的角色、负责人和每月预算，在频道里看得到对话，轮到它时才接话，干活过程所有人都能看见。

让 Agent 动手前先问一句，这个设计我觉得挺实在。

Agent 还有自己的电脑和浏览器。浏览器功能还在测试，操作时能在聊天里实时看着，碰到登录或验证码可以接手，弄完再交还。

repos.name: y5ez3g/facadecode
repos.description: The multi-agent orchestrator for VS Code. Run Claude Code, Codex, and other agent CLIs that start, message, and operate each other across windows and machines.

tweet.text:
this tool turn Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents into one team.

i just found an open-source tool that lets multiple AI coding agents collaborate, delegate tasks, and communicate with one another directly inside your IDE.

it’s called Facade Code.

and it’s already gaining attention, with 360+ GitHub stars.

here’s what makes it powerful:

→ run multiple agents: use Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Muse Code, OpenCode, and Pi side by side.

→ agents can manage other agents: one agent can start another, assign it a task, stop it, and send it instructions.

→ agent-to-agent communication: agents can message each other, read their terminal screens, and help unblock stuck agents.

→ parallel coding: give different agents separate tasks and let them work simultaneously.

→ Git worktree support: isolate different features and coding tasks so agents don’t interfere with each other’s changes.

→ track everything: monitor which agents are working, waiting for permission, or encountering errors.

→ cross-machine collaboration: connect agents across multiple VS Code windows and even remote machines through SSH.

→ use your existing accounts: each agent runs through its own CLI, login, and subscription.

here’s how to set it up:

1. install the Facade Code extension from the VS Code Marketplace.

2. or run:

code --install-extension facade.facadecode

1. install and sign in to the coding agents you want to use, such as Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode.

2. open Facade Code and start your agents from the Agent Panel.

3. assign tasks and let them collaborate on your project.

there’s more:

→ it also has a dedicated VS Code-based IDE preview for managing multiple projects and agent teams in one workspace.

→ supports macOS (Apple silicon), Linux (x64), and Windows (x64).

→ the extension is free and open source under the MIT license.

→ it uses MCP and a terminal protocol to let agents interact with one another.

important: agents run with approval prompts disabled by default through its yolo setting. They can execute commands and modify files without asking first. Turn this off if you want the normal approval safeguards.

repos.description: Kitesurf is an experimental browser engine that runs on Cloudflare Workers.

tweet.text:
🪁 Cloudflare 刚开源了 Kitesurf，让 agent 不用开 Chrome 也能打开网页、跑 JS、截图。

Kitesurf 是 Cloudflare 官方出品的实验项目，已经上了 Trendshift 日榜。

以前想让 agent 自动浏览网页，基本得起一个无头 Chrome 或者浏览器容器，又吃资源又难扩容。

Kitesurf 直接把浏览器引擎搬进了 Cloudflare Workers：解析 HTML、套 CSS、执行页面里的 JavaScript、渲染截图都在 Worker 里完成，每个页面跑在单独隔离的 worker 里。它支持 Chrome DevTools 协议，Puppeteer 这类客户端可以直接连上来用。

引擎底下拼的是一串开源 Rust 项目：Stylo 管 CSS，Boa 在 WebAssembly 里跑 JS，Krilla 还能顺手输出 PDF。

要说清楚的是：Kitesurf 目前还是实验性项目，要用到 Workers 付费计划里的 Dynamic Workers，自身也不带认证，部署后得自己在前面加一层访问控制。

给 agent 用的浏览器，正在从容器里搬到边缘节点上。

tweet.text:
4 FREE GITHUB REPOS TO GIVE GROK BOT A NERVOUS SYSTEM.

the concept: give it a goal, let several possible actions compete, and make the competition visible.

every input changes the state.
every candidate predicts a different outcome.
one action eventually wins.

the architecture i'd build around Grok:

01 / MEMORY — Graphiti
stores events and relationships with a timeline. what happened, what changed, what used to be true.

https://t.co/bbHwCUqx7L

02 / STATE — ncps
recurrent neural circuits inspired by biological nervous systems. incoming signals update a state that carries forward through time.

https://t.co/emYEiLFMLb

03 / FORESIGHT — pymdp
compares possible action sequences inside a model of the environment. sometimes the useful next move is gathering information.

https://t.co/mXd9LJxErj

04 / VISIBILITY — 3d-force-graph
the canvas for mapping inputs, connections, candidate actions and changing scores into a live network.

https://t.co/yzzsjeQU7w

Grok turns the instruction into a goal and candidate moves. these layers give those moves somewhere to be evaluated.

the decision layer gets seven outputs:

> preferred action
> probability of success
> risk to the agent
> risk to its target
> progress toward the goal
> change in resources
> execution intensity

then comes the interesting experiment:

keep the goal fixed.
change one input.

the target gets closer.
success becomes more likely.
resource cost rises.
risk crosses a limit.

the leading action starts losing its advantage. another candidate takes over. execution intensity drops before anything happens.

same objective. a different decision because the situation changed.

after the action, the result feeds back into memory and updates the next cycle.

observe -> predict -> compare -> act -> remember

you could pause at any point and ask:

which action was winning?
what changed its score?
what would have made another action win?

the most interesting output might be the action that almost happened. https://t.co/bMHAtzcu6F

repos.name: Liuzedooong/SparseReading
repos.description: Saving your tokens 🔥! SparseRead enables AI agents to selectively read what matters across diverse information sources.

tweet.text:
Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences cut AI-agent token consumption by up to 92.9%, without retraining a single model.

They also reduced execution time by up to 89%.

The problem is familiar if you've built AI agents. Ask a coding agent to investigate one error, and it may read an entire log, repository file, or document when only a few passages are relevant.

Those unnecessary tokens can remain in context across subsequent model calls, increasing cost and latency.

The researchers developed SparseRead, a system that controls what an agent reads before the content enters the model's context.

It works through three components →

1./ Read Intent Protocol: Tracks what information the agent needs, which evidence has been found, and what remains unresolved.

2./ Adaptive Reader Backends: Locate relevant evidence across documents, PDFs, code repositories, and structured data.

3./ Budgeted Read Gate: Limits how much source content enters context, with the option to fall back to reading the complete file.

Across six models and five workload scenarios, the researchers reported →
> Up to 92.9% fewer tokens consumed.
> Up to 89% less execution time.
> Median reductions of 61.4% in tokens and 53.7% in time.
> Task quality preserved or improved in most evaluated settings.

No model retraining is required.

The interesting engineering lesson is that context optimization doesn't have to begin with compression or KV caching.

You can reduce a substantial amount of work by controlling what enters the context in the first place.

(Link to the paper and code in comments)

repos.name: snarktank/ralph
repos.description: Ralph is an autonomous AI agent loop that runs repeatedly until all PRD items are complete.

tweet.text:
This is insane. The full stack for agents that run in loops and graphs is already on GitHub, and every piece of it is free.

Prompting gets you a chatbot. These 8 repos turn it into a system that checks its own work and calls you only for the step that matters.

Here’s the order to put it together ↓

Ralph → the loop that won’t stop until the work is done.

Turns your PRD into a list of stories with a passes flag each, then runs Claude Code or Amp again and again until every story passes. Each pass starts with fresh context and remembers only git, progress.txt and prd.json.
↳ https://t.co/pAFvCNQXIG

mini-swe-agent → the whole agent loop in about 100 lines.
No tools except bash, one linear history, one command per step. Read it once and you’ll see what every coding agent does underneath.
↳ https://t.co/uoE6SOTQ2l

promptfoo → the check your loop runs against.
Tests prompts, agents and RAG pipelines and runs those checks in CI, so the loop has something that can actually fail.
↳ https://t.co/2jkNmtoTUJ

Google ADK → loops and graphs in one Python toolkit.

Its workflow runtime is a graph engine with routing, fan-out and fan-in, loops and retries, so you compose agents instead of writing one long prompt.
↳ https://t.co/U1V6b30FXt

Microsoft Agent Framework → graph workflows that can rewind.
Sequential, concurrent and handoff patterns with checkpointing, human-in-the-loop and time travel, in Python and .NET.

↳ https://t.co/8PKJ5eFtmZ
Mastra → the gate where a workflow waits for you.
A TypeScript graph engine with sequential, conditional and parallel steps, and any workflow can pause until you approve, then pick up from there.
↳ https://t.co/oGEaJ4Yfmw

Temporal → loops that survive a crash.
A durable execution platform, so a long-running job continues from where it stopped after a restart instead of starting over.
↳ https://t.co/u0fNUHLa01

Phoenix → see what every node actually did.
OpenTelemetry tracing and evals for LLM apps, with support for the Claude Agent SDK and the OpenAI Agents SDK.
↳ https://t.co/EXf9Jq6otA

Loop → Check → Graph → Gate → Recover → Observe.

Bookmark this before your next long agent run.

How these pieces fit into one system where you approve only one step is in my Loops & Graphs guide below ↓ Your agents can already work for hours without you

But you still check every step they take

Because you have a loop, but no graph

I broke down how to build a system where you only approve the last step ↓ https://t.co/x0Kg0o0Clp

repos.name: delef/ClamDown
repos.description: Keep coding agents working on a MacBook with the lid closed. Free menu bar app: no sleep, fan control by CPU temperature, screen lock, battery and heat cut-offs.

tweet.text:
让 Claude Code 跑一个长任务，人又要出门，MacBook 只能半开着盖子拎在手上，一合上任务就停了。

ClamDown 是一个 Mac 菜单栏小工具，打开开关后合上盖子也不睡眠，Agent、终端和下载都接着跑。

合盖时系统会把风扇压在低速，它会按 CPU 温度调风扇，默认 60 度以下最低速，到 85 度满速。合上的同时还会锁屏。

GitHub：https://t.co/RdnT316saZ

电量掉到 10%、机器过热或者定时结束，它会自己关掉开关让 Mac 正常睡眠，并发通知说明原因。

就算应用崩溃或退出，后台的辅助程序约 90 秒收不到心跳，也会把睡眠、低电量模式和风扇恢复原样。

免费开源，安装包经过苹果公证，macOS 13 及以上能用。合盖以后温度和电量都有人盯着，背着出门跑任务也放心多了。

tweet.text:
GitHub is a goldmine for music producers.

I found 10 insane repos that help you write, split, master and remix tracks, some with Claude and AI. All free.

Bookmark this for later:

1. Ableton MCP

Connect Claude to Ableton Live. Create tracks, arrange clips and compose music just by describing what you want.

https://t.co/NP47TZoYaK

2. ACE-Step 1.5

Generate full songs on your own computer, from short loops to 10-minute tracks, with lyrics in 50+ languages. Under 10 seconds per song on an RTX 3090.

https://t.co/Rl76BjNO0H

3. YuE2

Give it lyrics and a style. It writes the melody and chords first, then turns them into a complete song with vocals. It can also make covers in a new style.

https://t.co/vVTyS2iuCc

4. Ultimate Vocal Remover

Pull the vocals out of any song, or split it into stems, with neural networks. 27K+ stars.

https://t.co/0zChgUmutL

5. Basic Pitch

Spotify's free audio-to-MIDI converter. Play or sing a melody and get MIDI back, pitch bends included.

https://t.co/jzL9cMcZGX

6. Matchering

Master your track to sound like any reference song. It matches loudness, frequency response, peaks and stereo width.

https://t.co/aeJl1FC3Sn

7. Surge XT

A free, open-source hybrid synthesizer you can load as a plugin.

https://t.co/gjRpLodK8D

8. Dexed

The classic Yamaha DX7 FM synth, rebuilt as a free plugin.

https://t.co/37fbAGVX7g

9. VCV Rack

A virtual Eurorack modular studio on your computer.

https://t.co/lhWK9kBAre

10. LMMS

A free, cross-platform music production app.

https://t.co/iAyGdHnIOx

还有个顺手的：仓库自带一个评审 skill，把你的 PRD、设计文档或 agent 代码丢给它，它先判断你做的是个人项目、团队工具还是面向客户的产品，再挑相关章节出报告，每条问题都带严重程度、证据、章节出处和修复建议。课程拿 OpenCode、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw、Paperclip 四个开源项目当参考实现。

tweet.text:
✨ 眼前一亮，Ryugi 让 Claude Code 这类编码 agent 把方案直接画在页面上给你看，你在哪里点、评了什么，反馈都原路回到那个会话。

Ryugi 的作者是 Innei，GitHub 主页写着在做 LobeHub；项目从 Superpowers v7.0.0 分出来，11 月 12 日一天就连发了四个版本。

以前让 agent 出个界面方案或设计思路，它只能在终端里用文字描述，你脑补半天，回一句「左边再窄一点」，它又重写一大段。

Ryugi 给了五种页面：画板、文档、白板、HTML 和验证页。agent 把方案画出来，你直接在页面上选中、评论，点通过或驳回，裁决回到创建页面的那个 agent 会话。东西都存在你自己的项目里，由本地服务器打开，要分享再生成链接。

验证页也挺实在：agent 说「做完了」时，会逐条列出它跑了什么来核实、附上原始输出，没验证的也单独列出来并写明原因。

Ryugi 会替换 Claude 自带的托管 Artifacts，Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 等也能用。要留意它现在用的是自定义的源码可见许可，不是开源许可。

让 agent 少说多画，你也少猜一点。

repos.name: Omodaka9375/browserr
repos.description: Servo-based headless browser engine for AI agents. An auditable alternative to embedding Chromium.

tweet.text:
给 Agent 用的浏览器，不用再套 Chromium 了

Browserr 刚开源，是个跑在 Servo 上的无头浏览器引擎，专门给 AI 智能体用的

它不走 CDP 那套上千个接口，整个协议就 22 条命令，JSON 走本地回环，一个下午能审计完

MCP 是原生的，直接给 42 个工具，Claude、Codex 这些能接 MCP 的客户端不用写集成代码就能用

一个二进制文件大概 120MB，零依赖，默认 CPU 渲染，没显卡的机器、容器、树莓派都能跑

设计上是 fail-closed，不确定的请求先拦下来，5 秒没人拍板就拒绝，付钱和验证码必须人来确认

验证码、一次性码、付款页面能自动识别，pause 一下把页面交还给真人，截图上每个元素都编了号，人和智能体指着同一个东西说话

每次操作都留证据，带时间戳的截图加一份只追加的操作日志

React 18 和 Vue 3 都能跑，Windows、Linux、macOS 都有包，Python 3.10 以上就能用

刚开源 4 天，仓库在 Omodaka9375/browserr，Apache-2.0 协议

motion, prototypes, websites and apps with an agent. local-first and open source.

https://t.co/fP6OdiPJ2e

critique, audit, polish and catch the AI slop before your client does.

https://t.co/4dx2KTn9DY

built for agents. your promo is now a file, not a week of editing.

https://t.co/Qf1N49OLMF

it plans before it builds, tests its own work and debugs instead of guessing.

https://t.co/tG3IVC7i6P

turns code, docs, SQL and PDFs into a knowledge graph your agent can actually query.

https://t.co/dnVrDGzFZG

research, forms, dashboards. it clicks so you don't have to.

https://t.co/N3wTb6jn47

one tool for Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Sheets and Docs.

every repo here is public. your competitor just has to find this post before you do.

tweet.text:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL GOLDMINE FOR EVERY AI BUILDER

18 open source repos to run a whole team of agents. 202 ready-made agents, 185 skills, official agent frameworks from OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and AWS, plus memory, sandboxes, tracing and training:

Run many coding agents at once

Claude Squad (8.8k stars): run several Claude Code or Codex sessions in one terminal, each in its own copy of the repo
https://t.co/g1bA2Dx0BE

Vibe Kanban (28.7k stars): a task board where you hand each task to a coding agent and review what it changed
https://t.co/57YeVbAvnu

Ruflo (81.6k stars): turns Claude Code and Codex into a swarm of agents working together
https://t.co/LtmAG0JHzC

wshobson/agents (42.5k stars): 202 agents and 185 skills ready to drop into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor
https://t.co/n8KpjKFgcU

Build your own swarm

OpenAI Agents SDK (30.7k stars): OpenAI’s simple framework where agents pass tasks to each other, with safety checks and logs built in
https://t.co/KgoJkdWBB9

Google ADK (22.2k stars): Google’s kit to build agents in code, test them, deploy them and combine them into teams that split up work
https://t.co/UKUTlFbNQf

Microsoft Agent Framework (14.7k stars): Microsoft’s framework for single agents and multi-agent workflows, in Python and .NET
https://t.co/S20pCnvxNM

Strands Agents (9.2k stars): AWS’s SDK with limits, memory and multi-agent patterns in one package, works with any model
https://t.co/sn6LGCN8Le

CrewAI (60.9k stars): give each agent a role and a goal, and they work as a crew
https://t.co/5T4EincLH9

LangGraph Swarm (1.6k stars): agents hand control to whichever one fits the next step
https://t.co/n0AKx4PeLA

Let agents talk to each other

A2A (26.5k stars): an open standard, started at Google, so agents from different frameworks can work together
https://t.co/3ZiIkqSi6K

Give them a safe place to run

E2B (14.8k stars): sandboxes where agents run code without touching your machine
https://t.co/MA0CAdKABE

See what the swarm actually did

Langfuse (37.4k stars): every step, tool call and cost of every agent
https://t.co/YwMUhHLOqg

Phoenix (12.3k stars): find exactly where a run went wrong
https://t.co/3fNTs3TCCi

Shared memory

mem0 (68.9k stars): agents remember users and context between sessions
https://t.co/6pKfJxsJ8p

Letta (25.4k stars): agents with long-term memory that learn over time
https://t.co/dgvJULnIfJ

Train and test

ART (10.9k stars): train your agents on your own tasks with reinforcement learning
https://t.co/Z9LHYGDIfM

OASIS (5.4k stars): simulate up to a million agents on a social network
https://t.co/0J2cgcD2AZ Anthropic's agent team beat a single agent by 90%. Cursor's built a browser in a week. Other big labs are moving the same way.

This is how they work, and how you can run one today. https://t.co/ZryIeBcIFa

repos.name: aehyok/pi-thirdparty-model-settings
repos.description: Pi 编程智能体扩展：通过 /dsf-config 在本地网页中配置第三方 API 服务商（baseUrl / apiKey / models）

tweet.text:
我没想到使用 Pi 又省钱，而且正确率还这么高，甚至高过了 Claude Code

刚好我最近用Pi 比较多，主要是因为我平常用终端多，再加上Pi 又是极简
加上可玩性非常的强，所以我陆续装了 11 个开源插件，挑出来分享一下

💡 基础体验

1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：输入 /dsf-config 打开本地网页，填 Base URL、API Key 和模型，保存后 /model 里马上能看到，不用重启。支持 OpenAI 兼容、Responses、Anthropic、Gemini 四种协议，还能从 /models 接口拉取模型列表，点选添加。
🔗 https://t.co/C3OaTTH2hw

2、pi-powerline-footer：Powerlevel10k 风格的状态栏。模型、思考档位、git 分支、context 占用、token 和费用一眼看清，context 超过 70% 变黄，超过 90% 变红。另外带 Alt+S 暂存输入、常驻 bash 模式，还能用 /vibe 自定义加载文案。
🔗 https://t.co/ltAMKikeef

3、pi-context-view：/context 用图展示 context 被哪些内容占用；/context injections 能看到平时看不到的 system prompt、工具定义和其他插件注入的内容。插件本身不占 context。
🔗 https://t.co/O7RfUffc50

🌐 能力扩展

4、pi-web-access：让 Pi 能联网，提供 web_search 和 fetch_content 两个工具。不配置也能用（默认走 Exa MCP），也接 Brave、Tavily、Kimi、博查等几十家搜索服务。GitHub 链接会直接 clone 到本地，能解析 PDF，配了 Gemini 还能看 YouTube 视频。
🔗 https://t.co/UoVMhQ0KfC

5、pi-mcp-adapter：省 token 的 MCP 接入方式。把几百个工具定义收成一个约 200 token 的 mcp 代理工具，server 用到时才启动，闲置 10 分钟自动关闭。Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 里配好的 MCP 可以一键导入。
🔗 https://t.co/QKGgWFMJWJ

6、pi-subagents：把任务派给子 Agent。内置 scout（读代码）、reviewer（审代码）、oracle（给第二意见）、worker（写代码）等角色，用自然语言说「用 reviewer 审一下这个 diff」就行，支持并行和后台运行。
🔗 https://t.co/wK4zNf0Zcl

🧭 工作流

7、plannotator：Agent 出计划时自动在浏览器打开，可以像批 PR 一样逐行批注，再一键把意见发回 Agent；也能 review 本地 diff 和 GitHub PR。安装命令是 pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension（包名和仓库名不一样），启动时加 --plan，或用 /plannotator-plan-mode 切换。
🔗 https://t.co/DPwMB33TxP

8、pi-lens：Agent 每次写入或修改文件，都会实时跑 LSP、linter、formatter 和结构规则检查，把问题直接反馈给 Agent，还能拦下没读过文件就动手改的操作。
🔗 https://t.co/9ryuZ81EJt

9、pi-intercom：同一台机器上的多个 Pi 会话之间互发消息（Alt+M），比如研究会话把结论直接交给执行会话；/handover 会把当前会话总结后交接给另一个会话。
🔗 https://t.co/nPB675bwad

🧪 进阶玩法

10、pi-autoresearch：自动实验循环，改代码、跑 benchmark，结果变好就保留，变差就回滚，一直循环下去。适合测试速度、包体积、构建时间这类有明确指标的优化。
🔗 https://t.co/DrPdDYG3m9

11、pi-purge：/purge 替换 Pi 内置的 system prompt，可以只用你自己的提示词运行，适合做 prompt 实验和对比。
🔗 https://t.co/Fy9dpjPSnI

🎯 新手怎么选

第一批，装上就能感觉到变化：
1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：用中转或第三方 API 的话，先装这个，不用手改 models.json
2、pi-powerline-footer：context 和费用一直显示在眼前
3、pi-web-access：不用配置就能联网，提升最直接

第二批，用顺手之后再装：
4、pi-context-view：开始在意 token 消耗时，用来排查占用
5、pi-subagents：一开始只用 reviewer 和 oracle 两个就够
6、plannotator：习惯先出计划再动手的人会很喜欢
7、pi-mcp-adapter：手上已经有 MCP 再装

暂时不用急：pi-lens（比较重，依赖各语言的 LSP 和 linter）、pi-intercom（多开会话才用得上）、pi-autoresearch（无人值守循环，烧 token，还会自动 commit）、pi-purge（拿掉了内置提示词，strict 模式下连 AGENTS.md 和 skills 都不加载）

第一批一键安装：
pi install npm:pi-thirdparty-model-settings
pi install npm:pi-powerline-footer
pi install npm:pi-web-access

⚠️ 几个提醒
· pi-mcp-adapter 装上后会自动关闭 Pi 自带的 MCP，卸载后要手动打开
· pi-autoresearch 建议在 .auto/config.json 里设置 maxIterations 上限，并在单独的分支里跑
· 插件以你的用户权限运行，装之前最好看一眼 README

最后插件不用装那么多，不用的一定要记得卸载，直接跟Pi讲就好了。

我觉得最简单的先把模型、状态栏、联网这三件事配好，Pi 就已经很顺手了。 我去，不可思议 Codex CLI 在 Harness 横评里排名第一

而作为极简的 Pi 在 Harness 横评里也干到第二了，把 Claude Code 都压在后面

我简单看了一下 FrontierHarness v1.1 这个榜单：21 个 Harness，配 Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 等 5 个开源模型，跑 62 道题，每题跑 4 次。

1、综合榜

Pi 综合通过率 72.8%，排第二，只输给 Codex CLI，Claude Code 在它后面。

Pi 这么强我倒不意外，反而 Codex CLI 排这么靠前我有点没想到。

2、更说明问题的是 DeepSeek 这一组

🔸 Pi + DeepSeek：通过率 80.3%，每成功一题 $0.057
🔸 DSH Minimal + DeepSeek：通过率 73.3%，每成功一题 $0.183

同一个模型，只是换了个 Harness，通过率高 7 个点，成本只有对方的三分之一左右。
这也是我最近一个月，把 DSH 换成了 Pi的一个原因，另一个原因就是 Pi是支持 CLI的，

repos.name: nicobailon/pi-powerline-footer
repos.description: Powerline-style status bar extension for pi coding agent

tweet.text:
我没想到使用 Pi 又省钱，而且正确率还这么高，甚至高过了 Claude Code

刚好我最近用Pi 比较多，主要是因为我平常用终端多，再加上Pi 又是极简
加上可玩性非常的强，所以我陆续装了 11 个开源插件，挑出来分享一下

💡 基础体验

1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：输入 /dsf-config 打开本地网页，填 Base URL、API Key 和模型，保存后 /model 里马上能看到，不用重启。支持 OpenAI 兼容、Responses、Anthropic、Gemini 四种协议，还能从 /models 接口拉取模型列表，点选添加。
🔗 https://t.co/C3OaTTH2hw

2、pi-powerline-footer：Powerlevel10k 风格的状态栏。模型、思考档位、git 分支、context 占用、token 和费用一眼看清，context 超过 70% 变黄，超过 90% 变红。另外带 Alt+S 暂存输入、常驻 bash 模式，还能用 /vibe 自定义加载文案。
🔗 https://t.co/ltAMKikeef

3、pi-context-view：/context 用图展示 context 被哪些内容占用；/context injections 能看到平时看不到的 system prompt、工具定义和其他插件注入的内容。插件本身不占 context。
🔗 https://t.co/O7RfUffc50

🌐 能力扩展

4、pi-web-access：让 Pi 能联网，提供 web_search 和 fetch_content 两个工具。不配置也能用（默认走 Exa MCP），也接 Brave、Tavily、Kimi、博查等几十家搜索服务。GitHub 链接会直接 clone 到本地，能解析 PDF，配了 Gemini 还能看 YouTube 视频。
🔗 https://t.co/UoVMhQ0KfC

5、pi-mcp-adapter：省 token 的 MCP 接入方式。把几百个工具定义收成一个约 200 token 的 mcp 代理工具，server 用到时才启动，闲置 10 分钟自动关闭。Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 里配好的 MCP 可以一键导入。
🔗 https://t.co/QKGgWFMJWJ

6、pi-subagents：把任务派给子 Agent。内置 scout（读代码）、reviewer（审代码）、oracle（给第二意见）、worker（写代码）等角色，用自然语言说「用 reviewer 审一下这个 diff」就行，支持并行和后台运行。
🔗 https://t.co/wK4zNf0Zcl

🧭 工作流

7、plannotator：Agent 出计划时自动在浏览器打开，可以像批 PR 一样逐行批注，再一键把意见发回 Agent；也能 review 本地 diff 和 GitHub PR。安装命令是 pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension（包名和仓库名不一样），启动时加 --plan，或用 /plannotator-plan-mode 切换。
🔗 https://t.co/DPwMB33TxP

8、pi-lens：Agent 每次写入或修改文件，都会实时跑 LSP、linter、formatter 和结构规则检查，把问题直接反馈给 Agent，还能拦下没读过文件就动手改的操作。
🔗 https://t.co/9ryuZ81EJt

9、pi-intercom：同一台机器上的多个 Pi 会话之间互发消息（Alt+M），比如研究会话把结论直接交给执行会话；/handover 会把当前会话总结后交接给另一个会话。
🔗 https://t.co/nPB675bwad

🧪 进阶玩法

10、pi-autoresearch：自动实验循环，改代码、跑 benchmark，结果变好就保留，变差就回滚，一直循环下去。适合测试速度、包体积、构建时间这类有明确指标的优化。
🔗 https://t.co/DrPdDYG3m9

11、pi-purge：/purge 替换 Pi 内置的 system prompt，可以只用你自己的提示词运行，适合做 prompt 实验和对比。
🔗 https://t.co/Fy9dpjPSnI

🎯 新手怎么选

第一批，装上就能感觉到变化：
1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：用中转或第三方 API 的话，先装这个，不用手改 models.json
2、pi-powerline-footer：context 和费用一直显示在眼前
3、pi-web-access：不用配置就能联网，提升最直接

第二批，用顺手之后再装：
4、pi-context-view：开始在意 token 消耗时，用来排查占用
5、pi-subagents：一开始只用 reviewer 和 oracle 两个就够
6、plannotator：习惯先出计划再动手的人会很喜欢
7、pi-mcp-adapter：手上已经有 MCP 再装

暂时不用急：pi-lens（比较重，依赖各语言的 LSP 和 linter）、pi-intercom（多开会话才用得上）、pi-autoresearch（无人值守循环，烧 token，还会自动 commit）、pi-purge（拿掉了内置提示词，strict 模式下连 AGENTS.md 和 skills 都不加载）

第一批一键安装：
pi install npm:pi-thirdparty-model-settings
pi install npm:pi-powerline-footer
pi install npm:pi-web-access

⚠️ 几个提醒
· pi-mcp-adapter 装上后会自动关闭 Pi 自带的 MCP，卸载后要手动打开
· pi-autoresearch 建议在 .auto/config.json 里设置 maxIterations 上限，并在单独的分支里跑
· 插件以你的用户权限运行，装之前最好看一眼 README

最后插件不用装那么多，不用的一定要记得卸载，直接跟Pi讲就好了。

我觉得最简单的先把模型、状态栏、联网这三件事配好，Pi 就已经很顺手了。 我去，不可思议 Codex CLI 在 Harness 横评里排名第一

而作为极简的 Pi 在 Harness 横评里也干到第二了，把 Claude Code 都压在后面

我简单看了一下 FrontierHarness v1.1 这个榜单：21 个 Harness，配 Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 等 5 个开源模型，跑 62 道题，每题跑 4 次。

1、综合榜

Pi 综合通过率 72.8%，排第二，只输给 Codex CLI，Claude Code 在它后面。

Pi 这么强我倒不意外，反而 Codex CLI 排这么靠前我有点没想到。

🔸 DSH Minimal + DeepSeek：通过率 73.3%，每成功一题 $0.183

⚠️ 最后提醒一下：测试还没全部跑完，排名后面可能还会变。

模型固然重要，但 Harness 选没选对，直接决定最后的效果和成本。还没用过 Pi 的朋友可以试试。 https://t.co/LIDs9sZ2ZA

· pi-autoresearch 建议在 .auto/config.json 里设置 maxIterations 上限，并在单独的分支里跑
· 插件以你的用户权限运行，装之前最好看一眼 README

最后插件不用装那么多，不用的一定要记得卸载，直接跟Pi讲就好了。

我觉得最简单的先把模型、状态栏、联网这三件事配好，Pi 就已经很顺手了。 我去，不可思议 Codex CLI 在 Harness 横评里排名第一

而作为极简的 Pi 在 Harness 横评里也干到第二了，把 Claude Code 都压在后面

我简单看了一下 FrontierHarness v1.1 这个榜单：21 个 Harness，配 Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 等 5 个开源模型，跑 62 道题，每题跑 4 次。

1、综合榜

Pi 综合通过率 72.8%，排第二，只输给 Codex CLI，Claude Code 在它后面。

Pi 这么强我倒不意外，反而 Codex CLI 排这么靠前我有点没想到。

2、更说明问题的是 DeepSeek 这一组

🔸 Pi + DeepSeek：通过率 80.3%，每成功一题 $0.057
🔸 DSH Minimal + DeepSeek：通过率 73.3%，每成功一题 $0.183

同一个模型，只是换了个 Harness，通过率高 7 个点，成本只有对方的三分之一左右。
这也是我最近一个月，把 DSH 换成了 Pi的一个原因，另一个原因就是 Pi是支持 CLI的，
而 DSH 只有web和客户端，我平常基本全是CLI，而且方便调度。

3、我自己的体感

我日常用得最多的 Agent 就三个：Claude Code 和 Pi Agent和Codex CLI。
token如果实在不够用了，我就用一下 Grok build 和 antigravity。

Pi 的框架和设计都是极简模式，默认只有四个基础工具，上限反而特别高。

在现有项目上改代码，我用 Pi Agent + 本地部署的 GLM，比在外面用 Claude Opus、Gemini Flash 还要指哪打哪。只要说清楚改什么、改哪里，基本都能完成得很好，体感非常强烈。

⚠️ 最后提醒一下：测试还没全部跑完，排名后面可能还会变。

模型固然重要，但 Harness 选没选对，直接决定最后的效果和成本。还没用过 Pi 的朋友可以试试。 https://t.co/LIDs9sZ2ZA

repos.name: nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter
repos.description: Token-efficient MCP adapter for Pi coding agent

tweet.text:
我没想到使用 Pi 又省钱，而且正确率还这么高，甚至高过了 Claude Code

刚好我最近用Pi 比较多，主要是因为我平常用终端多，再加上Pi 又是极简
加上可玩性非常的强，所以我陆续装了 11 个开源插件，挑出来分享一下

💡 基础体验

1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：输入 /dsf-config 打开本地网页，填 Base URL、API Key 和模型，保存后 /model 里马上能看到，不用重启。支持 OpenAI 兼容、Responses、Anthropic、Gemini 四种协议，还能从 /models 接口拉取模型列表，点选添加。
🔗 https://t.co/C3OaTTH2hw

2、pi-powerline-footer：Powerlevel10k 风格的状态栏。模型、思考档位、git 分支、context 占用、token 和费用一眼看清，context 超过 70% 变黄，超过 90% 变红。另外带 Alt+S 暂存输入、常驻 bash 模式，还能用 /vibe 自定义加载文案。
🔗 https://t.co/ltAMKikeef

3、pi-context-view：/context 用图展示 context 被哪些内容占用；/context injections 能看到平时看不到的 system prompt、工具定义和其他插件注入的内容。插件本身不占 context。
🔗 https://t.co/O7RfUffc50

🌐 能力扩展

4、pi-web-access：让 Pi 能联网，提供 web_search 和 fetch_content 两个工具。不配置也能用（默认走 Exa MCP），也接 Brave、Tavily、Kimi、博查等几十家搜索服务。GitHub 链接会直接 clone 到本地，能解析 PDF，配了 Gemini 还能看 YouTube 视频。
🔗 https://t.co/UoVMhQ0KfC

5、pi-mcp-adapter：省 token 的 MCP 接入方式。把几百个工具定义收成一个约 200 token 的 mcp 代理工具，server 用到时才启动，闲置 10 分钟自动关闭。Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 里配好的 MCP 可以一键导入。
🔗 https://t.co/QKGgWFMJWJ

6、pi-subagents：把任务派给子 Agent。内置 scout（读代码）、reviewer（审代码）、oracle（给第二意见）、worker（写代码）等角色，用自然语言说「用 reviewer 审一下这个 diff」就行，支持并行和后台运行。
🔗 https://t.co/wK4zNf0Zcl

🧭 工作流

7、plannotator：Agent 出计划时自动在浏览器打开，可以像批 PR 一样逐行批注，再一键把意见发回 Agent；也能 review 本地 diff 和 GitHub PR。安装命令是 pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension（包名和仓库名不一样），启动时加 --plan，或用 /plannotator-plan-mode 切换。
🔗 https://t.co/DPwMB33TxP

8、pi-lens：Agent 每次写入或修改文件，都会实时跑 LSP、linter、formatter 和结构规则检查，把问题直接反馈给 Agent，还能拦下没读过文件就动手改的操作。
🔗 https://t.co/9ryuZ81EJt

9、pi-intercom：同一台机器上的多个 Pi 会话之间互发消息（Alt+M），比如研究会话把结论直接交给执行会话；/handover 会把当前会话总结后交接给另一个会话。
🔗 https://t.co/nPB675bwad

🧪 进阶玩法

10、pi-autoresearch：自动实验循环，改代码、跑 benchmark，结果变好就保留，变差就回滚，一直循环下去。适合测试速度、包体积、构建时间这类有明确指标的优化。
🔗 https://t.co/DrPdDYG3m9

11、pi-purge：/purge 替换 Pi 内置的 system prompt，可以只用你自己的提示词运行，适合做 prompt 实验和对比。
🔗 https://t.co/Fy9dpjPSnI

🎯 新手怎么选

第一批，装上就能感觉到变化：
1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：用中转或第三方 API 的话，先装这个，不用手改 models.json
2、pi-powerline-footer：context 和费用一直显示在眼前
3、pi-web-access：不用配置就能联网，提升最直接

第二批，用顺手之后再装：
4、pi-context-view：开始在意 token 消耗时，用来排查占用
5、pi-subagents：一开始只用 reviewer 和 oracle 两个就够
6、plannotator：习惯先出计划再动手的人会很喜欢
7、pi-mcp-adapter：手上已经有 MCP 再装

暂时不用急：pi-lens（比较重，依赖各语言的 LSP 和 linter）、pi-intercom（多开会话才用得上）、pi-autoresearch（无人值守循环，烧 token，还会自动 commit）、pi-purge（拿掉了内置提示词，strict 模式下连 AGENTS.md 和 skills 都不加载）

第一批一键安装：
pi install npm:pi-thirdparty-model-settings
pi install npm:pi-powerline-footer
pi install npm:pi-web-access

· pi-mcp-adapter 装上后会自动关闭 Pi 自带的 MCP，卸载后要手动打开
· pi-autoresearch 建议在 .auto/config.json 里设置 maxIterations 上限，并在单独的分支里跑
· 插件以你的用户权限运行，装之前最好看一眼 README

🔗 https://t.co/Fy9dpjPSnI

🎯 新手怎么选

第一批，装上就能感觉到变化：
1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：用中转或第三方 API 的话，先装这个，不用手改 models.json
2、pi-powerline-footer：context 和费用一直显示在眼前
3、pi-web-access：不用配置就能联网，提升最直接

第二批，用顺手之后再装：
4、pi-context-view：开始在意 token 消耗时，用来排查占用
5、pi-subagents：一开始只用 reviewer 和 oracle 两个就够
6、plannotator：习惯先出计划再动手的人会很喜欢
7、pi-mcp-adapter：手上已经有 MCP 再装

暂时不用急：pi-lens（比较重，依赖各语言的 LSP 和 linter）、pi-intercom（多开会话才用得上）、pi-autoresearch（无人值守循环，烧 token，还会自动 commit）、pi-purge（拿掉了内置提示词，strict 模式下连 AGENTS.md 和 skills 都不加载）

第一批一键安装：
pi install npm:pi-thirdparty-model-settings
pi install npm:pi-powerline-footer
pi install npm:pi-web-access

⚠️ 几个提醒
· pi-mcp-adapter 装上后会自动关闭 Pi 自带的 MCP，卸载后要手动打开
· pi-autoresearch 建议在 .auto/config.json 里设置 maxIterations 上限，并在单独的分支里跑
· 插件以你的用户权限运行，装之前最好看一眼 README

最后插件不用装那么多，不用的一定要记得卸载，直接跟Pi讲就好了。

我觉得最简单的先把模型、状态栏、联网这三件事配好，Pi 就已经很顺手了。 我去，不可思议 Codex CLI 在 Harness 横评里排名第一

而作为极简的 Pi 在 Harness 横评里也干到第二了，把 Claude Code 都压在后面

我简单看了一下 FrontierHarness v1.1 这个榜单：21 个 Harness，配 Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 等 5 个开源模型，跑 62 道题，每题跑 4 次。

1、综合榜

Pi 综合通过率 72.8%，排第二，只输给 Codex CLI，Claude Code 在它后面。

Pi 这么强我倒不意外，反而 Codex CLI 排这么靠前我有点没想到。

2、更说明问题的是 DeepSeek 这一组

🔸 Pi + DeepSeek：通过率 80.3%，每成功一题 $0.057
🔸 DSH Minimal + DeepSeek：通过率 73.3%，每成功一题 $0.183

同一个模型，只是换了个 Harness，通过率高 7 个点，成本只有对方的三分之一左右。
这也是我最近一个月，把 DSH 换成了 Pi的一个原因，另一个原因就是 Pi是支持 CLI的，
而 DSH 只有web和客户端，我平常基本全是CLI，而且方便调度。

3、我自己的体感

我日常用得最多的 Agent 就三个：Claude Code 和 Pi Agent和Codex CLI。
token如果实在不够用了，我就用一下 Grok build 和 antigravity。

Pi 的框架和设计都是极简模式，默认只有四个基础工具，上限反而特别高。

在现有项目上改代码，我用 Pi Agent + 本地部署的 GLM，比在外面用 Claude Opus、Gemini Flash 还要指哪打哪。只要说清楚改什么、改哪里，基本都能完成得很好，体感非常强烈。

⚠️ 最后提醒一下：测试还没全部跑完，排名后面可能还会变。

模型固然重要，但 Harness 选没选对，直接决定最后的效果和成本。还没用过 Pi 的朋友可以试试。 https://t.co/LIDs9sZ2ZA

tweet.text:
我没想到使用 Pi 又省钱，而且正确率还这么高，甚至高过了 Claude Code

刚好我最近用Pi 比较多，主要是因为我平常用终端多，再加上Pi 又是极简

🔗 https://t.co/C3OaTTH2hw

2、pi-powerline-footer：Powerlevel10k 风格的状态栏。模型、思考档位、git 分支、context 占用、token 和费用一眼看清，context 超过 70% 变黄，超过 90% 变红。另外带 Alt+S 暂存输入、常驻 bash 模式，还能用 /vibe 自定义加载文案。
🔗 https://t.co/ltAMKikeef

3、pi-context-view：/context 用图展示 context 被哪些内容占用；/context injections 能看到平时看不到的 system prompt、工具定义和其他插件注入的内容。插件本身不占 context。
🔗 https://t.co/O7RfUffc50

🌐 能力扩展

4、pi-web-access：让 Pi 能联网，提供 web_search 和 fetch_content 两个工具。不配置也能用（默认走 Exa MCP），也接 Brave、Tavily、Kimi、博查等几十家搜索服务。GitHub 链接会直接 clone 到本地，能解析 PDF，配了 Gemini 还能看 YouTube 视频。
🔗 https://t.co/UoVMhQ0KfC

5、pi-mcp-adapter：省 token 的 MCP 接入方式。把几百个工具定义收成一个约 200 token 的 mcp 代理工具，server 用到时才启动，闲置 10 分钟自动关闭。Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 里配好的 MCP 可以一键导入。
🔗 https://t.co/QKGgWFMJWJ

6、pi-subagents：把任务派给子 Agent。内置 scout（读代码）、reviewer（审代码）、oracle（给第二意见）、worker（写代码）等角色，用自然语言说「用 reviewer 审一下这个 diff」就行，支持并行和后台运行。
🔗 https://t.co/wK4zNf0Zcl

🧭 工作流

7、plannotator：Agent 出计划时自动在浏览器打开，可以像批 PR 一样逐行批注，再一键把意见发回 Agent；也能 review 本地 diff 和 GitHub PR。安装命令是 pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension（包名和仓库名不一样），启动时加 --plan，或用 /plannotator-plan-mode 切换。
🔗 https://t.co/DPwMB33TxP

8、pi-lens：Agent 每次写入或修改文件，都会实时跑 LSP、linter、formatter 和结构规则检查，把问题直接反馈给 Agent，还能拦下没读过文件就动手改的操作。
🔗 https://t.co/9ryuZ81EJt

7、plannotator：Agent 出计划时自动在浏览器打开，可以像批 PR 一样逐行批注，再一键把意见发回 Agent；也能 review 本地 diff 和 GitHub PR。安装命令是 pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension（包名和仓库名不一样），启动时加 --plan，或用 /plannotator-plan-mode 切换。
🔗 https://t.co/DPwMB33TxP

8、pi-lens：Agent 每次写入或修改文件，都会实时跑 LSP、linter、formatter 和结构规则检查，把问题直接反馈给 Agent，还能拦下没读过文件就动手改的操作。
🔗 https://t.co/9ryuZ81EJt

9、pi-intercom：同一台机器上的多个 Pi 会话之间互发消息（Alt+M），比如研究会话把结论直接交给执行会话；/handover 会把当前会话总结后交接给另一个会话。
🔗 https://t.co/nPB675bwad

🧪 进阶玩法

10、pi-autoresearch：自动实验循环，改代码、跑 benchmark，结果变好就保留，变差就回滚，一直循环下去。适合测试速度、包体积、构建时间这类有明确指标的优化。
🔗 https://t.co/DrPdDYG3m9

11、pi-purge：/purge 替换 Pi 内置的 system prompt，可以只用你自己的提示词运行，适合做 prompt 实验和对比。
🔗 https://t.co/Fy9dpjPSnI

🎯 新手怎么选

第一批，装上就能感觉到变化：
1、pi-thirdparty-model-settings：用中转或第三方 API 的话，先装这个，不用手改 models.json
2、pi-powerline-footer：context 和费用一直显示在眼前
3、pi-web-access：不用配置就能联网，提升最直接

第二批，用顺手之后再装：
4、pi-context-view：开始在意 token 消耗时，用来排查占用
5、pi-subagents：一开始只用 reviewer 和 oracle 两个就够
6、plannotator：习惯先出计划再动手的人会很喜欢
7、pi-mcp-adapter：手上已经有 MCP 再装

暂时不用急：pi-lens（比较重，依赖各语言的 LSP 和 linter）、pi-intercom（多开会话才用得上）、pi-autoresearch（无人值守循环，烧 token，还会自动 commit）、pi-purge（拿掉了内置提示词，strict 模式下连 AGENTS.md 和 skills 都不加载）

第一批一键安装：
pi install npm:pi-thirdparty-model-settings
pi install npm:pi-powerline-footer
pi install npm:pi-web-access

⚠️ 几个提醒
· pi-mcp-adapter 装上后会自动关闭 Pi 自带的 MCP，卸载后要手动打开
· pi-autoresearch 建议在 .auto/config.json 里设置 maxIterations 上限，并在单独的分支里跑
· 插件以你的用户权限运行，装之前最好看一眼 README

最后插件不用装那么多，不用的一定要记得卸载，直接跟Pi讲就好了。

我觉得最简单的先把模型、状态栏、联网这三件事配好，Pi 就已经很顺手了。 我去，不可思议 Codex CLI 在 Harness 横评里排名第一

而作为极简的 Pi 在 Harness 横评里也干到第二了，把 Claude Code 都压在后面

我简单看了一下 FrontierHarness v1.1 这个榜单：21 个 Harness，配 Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 等 5 个开源模型，跑 62 道题，每题跑 4 次。

1、综合榜

Pi 综合通过率 72.8%，排第二，只输给 Codex CLI，Claude Code 在它后面。

Pi 这么强我倒不意外，反而 Codex CLI 排这么靠前我有点没想到。

2、更说明问题的是 DeepSeek 这一组

🔸 Pi + DeepSeek：通过率 80.3%，每成功一题 $0.057
🔸 DSH Minimal + DeepSeek：通过率 73.3%，每成功一题 $0.183

同一个模型，只是换了个 Harness，通过率高 7 个点，成本只有对方的三分之一左右。
这也是我最近一个月，把 DSH 换成了 Pi的一个原因，另一个原因就是 Pi是支持 CLI的，
而 DSH 只有web和客户端，我平常基本全是CLI，而且方便调度。

3、我自己的体感

我日常用得最多的 Agent 就三个：Claude Code 和 Pi Agent和Codex CLI。
token如果实在不够用了，我就用一下 Grok build 和 antigravity。

Pi 的框架和设计都是极简模式，默认只有四个基础工具，上限反而特别高。

在现有项目上改代码，我用 Pi Agent + 本地部署的 GLM，比在外面用 Claude Opus、Gemini Flash 还要指哪打哪。只要说清楚改什么、改哪里，基本都能完成得很好，体感非常强烈。

⚠️ 最后提醒一下：测试还没全部跑完，排名后面可能还会变。

模型固然重要，但 Harness 选没选对，直接决定最后的效果和成本。还没用过 Pi 的朋友可以试试。 https://t.co/LIDs9sZ2ZA

repos.name: oil-oil/agy-fast-io
repos.description: 让 Antigravity 少走回合、少等审查的本地规则插件（非官方）

tweet.text:
最近非常高强度地使用了 Antigravity 和 Gemini 模型，说说自己的感受和一些实用技巧：

1. 在 Gemini 4 Carbon 出来之前，我一直用的是 Gemini 4 Argon。200 刀套餐的额度很多，在我重度开发、适当搭配 Codex 进行 review 的情况下，周额度到最后一两天还得单独搞点重活才能用得完，所以大多数情况下可以爽用。现在 Gemini 4 Carbon 出来之后，任务效果比 Argon 更好，并且消耗并没有高多少，几乎和之前使用 Argon 是一样的。

但是即便是 Gemini 4 Carbon，我自己的感受也是不如 使用 Claude Opus 5.5 的。Claude 给人的感觉是心思更加缜密，更加让人安心。比如在一个复杂仓库里面，一些分支管理、版本管理这些都是 Claude 会更稳定，而且它会主动告诉你当前存在什么问题，审美和开发能力也还是 Claude 更强。

Gemini 的优势在于订阅门槛很低，而且比起 Codex 来说，交流感好太多了，文案能力也强。如果平时需要让 AI 辅助写写课程、做做视频脚本，那么 Gemini 是目前唯一的选择。

2. Gemini 4 不同的型号都是比较自信的模型，所以它给的方案以及它写的代码，经常缺胳膊少腿，它自己就觉得很不错，结果给其他模型看完了发现一大堆问题。

而且虽然说话有人味儿，但是会过度浮夸，喜欢加很多拟人、形容、比喻，给你很多情绪价值。如果用来开发复杂项目，一定要搭配其他的模型来帮助它 review，比如说另一个极端的 GPT。我自己一直都是用 GPT 来帮助 Gemini 评审方案和代码的，搭配起来使用效果非常好。

3. Antigravity 的 harness 很垃圾，读文件速度巨慢。而且如果我们开的是 Turbo 模式，虽然很多工具调用不会征求我们人的同意，但它一定会走一下云端审核，甚至很多读文件的命令都需要审核。

这个云端审核每一次大概 1 到 3 秒，你在执行一个复杂任务的时候，有可能审核好几十次，就会浪费好几分钟的时间用于这个云端审核。而且 Antigravity 读文件也不够高效，每一次读完文件都得思考，然后再去读下一个文件；单个文件读了几行，它还得思考完再读后面的几行；还有就是每一次任务完成的回答都是非常长的。

为了解决这个问题，我自己写了一个 Antigravity 的插件，整理了不需要走审核的白名单命令，并且提供了一些提示词，告诉 Antigravity 怎么样去高效地读代码：https://t.co/qSaMQ5yXWo

4. Gemini 4 Hydrogen 发布之后，也能够一定程度解决 Antigravity 读文件速度慢的问题。Antigravity 原生的子 Agent 仅支持 inherit / flash_lite / flash / pro 四个档位，这里竟然没有 Gemini 4 系列的模型。

但是 Antigravity 内部有一个叫做 swarm 的 Skill，相当于一个多 Agent 协作系统，这个 Skill 支持派发任何模型的子 Agent，甚至可以派发 Antigravity 里面的 Claude 模型。我的做法是通过我自己开发的另一个 Skill 套件 oil-dev-skills（https://t.co/PpWpMIgIcp），里面有一个 oil-explore，我们把 Antigravity 需要使用 swarm + Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Low) 探索代码作为规则配进去，后续在新的项目里面新开话题的时候，探索代码的速度就会非常快。

5. Antigravity 里面还有一个 Orchestrator 模式（比如 Orchestrator Carbon），它的机制其实就是计划模式，先用能力强的模型去探索代码、写方案，然后再让比较便宜的模型，比如说 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 去基于方案执行，但是现阶段对我来说，我觉得 Carbon 写代码尚有提升空间，更何况 Hydrogen 了，所以我会先在一些简单的项目里面测一下，现在测试得还不够多，所以不给大家结论

这个模式对单纯读文件、问问题其实没有加速帮助，因为读代码全在第一阶段，跑的还是最慢的规划模型，平时只看代码直接选 swarm + Hydrogen 反而更快。

repos.name: ModernRelay/omnigraph
repos.description: Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology

tweet.text:
Every AI company I've talked to is solving the same problem:

How to let several agents write to the same data without one silently undoing another's work?

Omnigraph is an open-source graph database that versions data the way developers already version code:

↳ Each agent writes on its own branch
↳ Omnigraph checks every merge against the latest main
↳ A policy blocks direct writes to main

GitHub repo: https://t.co/WBovu3DeOi

(don't forget to star it 🌟)

To test this, I gave Codex and Claude Code one shared graph of services and teams, with one task each, as shown in the video below:

- Codex moved a service from RabbitMQ to Kafka.
- Claude Code handed that same service's on-call to a new engineer.

Both agents started from the same version of that service.

Codex merged cleanly, but Claude Code got flagged for a conflict, rebuilt its change on the latest main, and then merged.

A row lock only helps when two agents hit the same record at the same moment.

But an agent's task usually touches many records over several minutes. A branch keeps that whole change isolated until it merges, and each merge leaves a diff you can review and a history of who changed what.

Omnigraph is written in Rust, and agents connect to it over MCP.

I shared the GitHub repo above.

To dive deeper, I wrote a full breakdown of why shared agent data needs branches, diffs, and merge checks, not just row locks.

It walks through a real run with two Claude Code agents, from the refused merge to the clean retry. Read it below.

Read it below. https://t.co/Qks4NHoghv

repos.name: rowboatlabs/rowboat
repos.description: Your agent team, in one group chat.

tweet.text:
An open-source, self-hostable layer that turns your agents into a team working toward shared goals.

It's called Rowboat, and it can bring Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes into one team. Any agent that supports MCP can join too, so you stop being the glue between your AI agents.

You send one message, and a super agent:

- Decides which agents the job needs
- Asks your permission and creates them
- Hands each one a task
- Lets them pass work along in threads
- Builds the result with them on a shared whiteboard

What makes it different:

↳ Runs on the subscriptions or API keys you already have
↳ See every handoff, and step in whenever you want
↳ Or let Rowboat host your agents, if you'd rather not run servers
↳ Free to use

The video below shows it in action.

I loaded nine weeks of product data for a sample app into PostHog, a product analytics tool, and asked the super agent why new users weren't coming back. Hermes found where they dropped off in PostHog, Claude Code found why in the user feedback, and Codex built the dashboard.

Link to the GitHub repo in the first comment.

tweet.text:
要说真正的逆向利器，还得是 Ghidra，光冲这背景就够猛的：它可是 NSA 给开源出来的逆向工程工具。

你随便拿个没源码的 ELF、EXE 这类二进制程序，直接往里一丢，它就能给你反汇编、反编译，把那些难啃的机器码尽量还原成人能看懂的伪代码，连函数图、调用关系等各种分析本事也一并备齐了。

眼下连逆向都开始往 Agent 那路子上靠了。社区里已经冒出了 ghidra-mcp、GhidraMCP 这类项目，能把 Codex、Claude Code 等 AI Agent 塞进 Ghidra 里，帮着去分析函数、交叉引用还有程序逻辑。

以前搞逆向，全靠人死盯着汇编一点点硬啃，如今渐渐演变成：Ghidra 负责拆解程序，AI 替你读。

像是做恶意样本分析、漏洞研究、CTF 或者给自家软件做安全审计，这玩意儿基本绕不过去。使的时候只管去分析你有权研究的那些软件跟样本。

以前查番号：复制 → 搜一下 → 翻封面 → 瞧排名，整套动作下来得来回横跳折腾。

如今avRanking Extension，瞅见番号点一下浏览器图标，就能直接匹配 JavRanking 的封面跟排行榜数据，用不着再开上一大堆页面。

隐私这块：按项目的说法，非得你主动点扩展图标它才会去读当前页面，浏览历史、URL 加上番号一概不存，也不会往外传。

安装不费劲：去 Releases 下个 ZIP → 解压 → 浏览器里打开开发者模式 →「加载已解压的扩展程序」。

就为查个封面，犯不着顺手把浏览记录也一并交出去。

🔗：https://t.co/n2rkWLrcq3

CLAUDE.md

FEATURES.md
HANDOFF.md
roles/PLANNER.md
roles/BUILDER.md
roles/EVALUATOR.md

your idea → feature contract → working app → browser checks → next feature

> the BUILDER finishes one agreed feature and runs the relevant checks
> the EVALUTOR tests the running product in a separate session and sends reproducible failures back

explicit code ownership + approval boundaries
finish the approved work before handing it back
review carried-over instructions instead of stacking more rules

feature status, check evidence, and the next action stay in your repo between sessions

repos.description: Claude Code plugin for creating LLM-as-a-judge evaluators using the Plurai platform

tweet.text:
This is the easiest way to build your first AI agent:

Step 1. Pick one task.
Choose one boring thing you do every day. Answering the same customer emails, booking calls, sorting leads. One task - one agent.

Step 2. Write the rules like you're training a new hire.
Open a note and write down:

> what comes in (an email, a form, a message)
> what the agent should do with it, step by step
> what a good result looks like
> what it should never do on its own (send money, delete things, promise refunds)

Step 3. Let Claude Code build it.
Open Claude Code in a new project folder and paste:

"Build me an agent that does [your task]. Here are the rules: [paste your note]. It should ask me before anything on the never list."

It writes the agent and connects the tools it needs.

Step 4. Test it before anyone else uses it.
This is the step almost everyone skips. Your agent can say "done, I booked it" while nothing got booked.

Connect Plurai to Claude Code. It's a free plugin that tests your agent before real users do: it builds a copy of your agent's world from your code, sends fake users who argue and go off topic, and checks what your agent actually did, not just what it said.

In Claude Code, in your agent's folder, paste these two lines:

/plugin marketplace add plurai-ai/plurai-plugins
/plugin install plurai-simulation@plurai-plugins

Then run:

/simulate [path to your agent]

The first time, it opens your browser to sign in.

Step 5. Fix what broke.
For every failure, Plurai shows you the conversation where it happened and the line of code behind it, and gives you the fix. Apply it and run /simulate again.

Step 6. Ship it.
Start with a few real users, watch what it does for a week, then let it run.

Your first agent is done. And the same steps work for any task you want to hand off: pick it, write the rules, build, test, fix, ship. Big day for us at @pluraiAI ! Plurai Simulation is live and free for every AI engineer.

AI agents look great in demos. Until real users break them.

So we built a world where your agent can fail, learn, and get fixed before your users ever see it.

→ Digital twin: Your real agent, its tools, and environment recreated from your code

→ Simulated users & tasks: Realistic users, tasks, and workflows that push your agent into the edge cases that matter

→ Auto evals: Check what your agent actually did, not just what it said

→ Verified fixes: Every failure comes with the run that exposed it and a fix you can verify

→ Replays: Turn any production failure into a simulation and replay it against every new version of your agent

All inside the coding agent you already use: @claudeai code, @OpenAICodexCli , or @GitHubCopilot .

Start simulating for free: https://t.co/1PNPQdW29S

17. Root Agent → 一个协调者，先判断请求需要哪些专家，再分派任务，把具体领域的活交给负责人

https://t.co/0P8uzOjJVx

19. Grok Bot Templates → 49 个模板，职责、产出、技能、例行任务和边界都写好了，还有能直接改成自己用的团队配置
https://t.co/iQgTKenJ9m

20. HyperGrok Trading Desk → 七个机器人，覆盖行情、研究、策略、风控、执行和复盘。默认从研究模式起步，实盘交易要你点头
https://t.co/K63c2RPRBi

repos.name: renezander030/capcut-cli
repos.description: Independent, unofficial CLI to edit CapCut and JianYing (剪映) projects — subtitles, timing, speed, volume, templates, cut long-form to shorts. No API needed, reads draft_content.json and draft_info.json (剪映草稿) directly. Not affiliated with ByteDance.

tweet.text:
爱用剪映的兄弟们呢，这工具真该装一个：capcut-cli，它能直接让你在终端里使唤 Claude Code / Codex 帮你剪视频。

是个非官方的剪映 / CapCut 命令行工具，牛的一点在于它能直接读写你本地的草稿。等 Agent 剪完之后，你再打开剪映一瞧，音频、视频还有字幕那些轨道全都能接着编辑，想怎么手动精修都成。

把原视频扔进去 → 它自己把静音和空白部分给删了 → 用 Whisper 整出字幕 → 自动把字幕样式套上 → 最后直接把剪映草稿生成出来。

到头来你只需打开剪映瞅一眼，再自己点个导出就完事了。

脏活累活全甩给 AI 去干，最后精修那步再交给剪映，这才是让 Agent 帮忙剪视频最舒服的玩法。

🔗：https://t.co/5LeWPja070

repos.name: yetone/magpie
repos.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

tweet.text:
开源工具：Magpie，这东西完全能当成 AI Coding Agent 的“模型总管”。

repos.name: NVIDIA-NeMo/labs-molt
repos.description: A scalable, agentic-first, and HuggingFace-native RL framework for research (9k lines).

tweet.text:
NVIDIA released a new RL framework:

Your entire setup is one Python file:

- write a class with a step() function
- return a reward from it
- the framework handles the rest, up to 1T-class MoE training

In a typical RL framework, the environment and reward logic are added inside the trainer's codebase.

Adding a new task requires writing framework code, registering it, and wiring up config for it.

The reward usually comes from a separately trained reward model, which needs its own GPUs and placement next to the actor and critic.

NVIDIA's Molt framework drops both these requirements.

Every run takes an agent_path flag pointing to one Python module, and the trainer code never changes.

The module gives you two ways to plug in an agent.

> The first is an Env class where you write a step() function that receives the model's output and returns a reward, and the framework handles everything else, i.e., calling the model, tokenizing, and looping turn after turn until the episode ends.

> The second is a ChatAgent class, for agents that already exist as their own loop. Here, you write the loop yourself, calling the model through a standard OpenAI or Anthropic client, and the framework spins up a local server so those calls hit its vLLM engines instead of an external API.

Either way, the trainer sees the same thing, i.e., a trajectory of tokens and a reward at the end.

That reward can come from a string-match grader, code executed in a sandboxed subprocess, or an LLM-as-judge call.

So there is no reward model to train or place, and no environment code living inside the framework.

Under the hood, Molt runs a single trainable actor (plus an optional critic for PPO) on FSDP2, vLLM engines for rollout, and Ray queues between them, so generation, training, and weight sync overlap instead of running in lockstep.

Scaling just requires setting some flags on the same command.

The framework also splits the model across GPUs for you, so the script that trains an 8B model on one node can also train DeepSeek-V3-scale MoE models on a cluster by raising the parallelism flags.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/TafSfatER5

Since the framework is new, I am still experimenting with it and will share more about my learnings soon.

To dive deeper into how top AI labs are building RL Agents in 2026, I wrote a full article about it.

It covers the evolution from RLHF to GRPO with verifiable rewards and using an LLM-as-judge reward function. This idea extends RL training to non-verifiable agentic tasks without writing custom reward functions.

Read it below.

https://t.co/mpVL03CCPZ

https://t.co/ypARyPni9r

4. 12-Factor Agents (27k). 12 principles for agents that hold up in production.
https://t.co/fmhPyFuoxV

https://t.co/C6Sr2DJJj8

6. Agents Towards Production (22k). 24 code-first tutorials: memory, MCP, security, tracing, deployment.
https://t.co/Qt5UXAl5sw

Couples agent and environments in a copy-on-write fork ~5x faster than docker commit, with ~95% KV-cache reuse on replay. Framework built for meta-agents to supervise, optimize, and train other agents

tweet.text:
Stanford researchers did it again.

They just built the agent-native version of Git.

When an agent works on a longer task, the run builds up a lot of state.

This includes files edited/created, a dev server, a database, installed packages, KV cache, etc.

Say the agent is at step 10 and makes a mistake, maybe it misreads a traceback and rewrites a file that was actually fine.

The tests start failing, and the run goes off track, although everything through step eight was correct.

By default, the agent just tries to fix it, which creates more edits and tool calls. This burns more tokens and grows the context.

The other options are a person stepping in to redirect it or restarting the whole run from step one.

That's wasteful, because it pays for every model/tool call again and re-prefills the context. Moreover, since an agent's run is non-deterministic, it doesn't reproduce the same early steps anyway.

The reason it's hard to just jump back exactly to a previous correct step and resume from there is that the trajectory is only a message log.

It records what the agent said and which tools it called, but not the live state underneath.

That state includes things like memory, open file handles, child processes, installed packages, /tmp, and KV cache. None of that is in the log.

Git can version the files, but it doesn't snapshot the running process or the KV cache. Checking out step eight moves the files back, but the process is still sitting in step-ten memory with a cold cache.

Shepherd is a runtime layer by Stanford that records the run as a trace of typed events rather than a flat log.

Each agent-environment interaction becomes a commit, similar to Git, but it tracks the live run.

Its commit includes the agent process and the filesystem together, copy-on-write, so a branch carries the actual state and not just the files.

Going back to a previous step is then a single call that forks from that commit and continues from the exact state.

The copy-on-write fork is roughly five times faster than docker commit, and because the prompt prefix through step eight is unchanged, the KV cache is reused over 95% on replay, so early steps aren't reprocessed again.

Once the run can be forked, a meta-agent can sit on top and operate it. It watches the trace and reverts as soon as it looks wrong, before the bad write is committed.

In practice, it's just Python calling fork, replay, and revert on the trace, rather than a separate control plane wired into the harness.

Not everything is reversible though.

Files and sandbox changes undo themselves, but a database write has no automatic undo, so it needs a matching undo step set up in advance.

Something external, like a sent email or a real charge, can't be undone, so the supervisor's job there is to catch it before it fires.

They tested this on a few public benchmarks. On CooperBench, where two agents work on the same codebase, adding a live supervisor took the pair-coding pass rate from 28.8% to 54.7%.

It's still early and labeled alpha. The benefit mostly shows up when a run gets branched a lot over a heavy sandbox state, which is exactly where restarting wastes the most tokens and time.

If Git was made to make file changes reversible, Shepherd is trying to do the same thing for a live agent run.

Shepherd Repo: https://t.co/uUIS57te6g

(don't forget to star it ⭐ )

That said, Shepherd reverts a bad step inside a run. The harness around it, the prompts, tools, and checks the supervisor relies on, still drifts across runs as models and dependencies change.

I wrote about making that harness repair itself, where a failing trace gets diagnosed, the fix is verified against the exact input that failed, and the failure is locked as a regression test so it can't recur. all of this is done using @Cometml's open-source project Opik.

The article is quoted below. https://t.co/YUGDPxpYvy

repos.description: A Claude Code skill to make motion design videos in pure code: HTML + Playwright + ffmpeg. No After Effects, no Remotion license.

tweet.text:
holy f*ck, opus 5.5 is getting dangerously close to replacing motion designers...

the problem is the video comes out looking like random animations stacked on top of each other.

these 6 repos turn claude into a full motion studio:

1. cinetic [https://t.co/Pl2xlT5tu9] -> makes claude direct a short film instead of stacking random animations. launch films, teasers, logo stings, ui walkthroughs.

2. earshot [https://t.co/7yAy4wFPAx] -> gives claude ears. 252 sound effects stored as code, claude listens to its own video and fixes the sync.

3. hyperframes (by heygen) [https://t.co/NgOCqhABN0] -> write html, get mp4. ~450 ready blocks: transitions, titles, charts, 3d. apache 2.0

4. remotion-dev/skills [https://t.co/crt6nEBnpK] -> 13 official remotion skills. captions, render, maps, multimedia.

5. claude-motion-design [https://t.co/at5Tmh7CLP] -> html + playwright + ffmpeg. remake mode: 1:1 copy of any launch video, rebuilt for your brand

6. lottiefiles motion-design [https://t.co/2DyccpHaNw] -> teaches claude timing, easing and choreography before it writes a single line of code

lottie plans the timing -> cinetic directs -> hyperframes or remotion renders -> earshot listens and fixes the sound

the trick isn't a smarter model. it's giving claude a director's brain, a sense of timing and a pair of ears.

no after effects. no stock sfx library. no motion designer on retainer. just opus 5.5, 6 repos and a loop.

bookmark this before you open after effects again.

Prompt : Create a 2D anime short for the web. It must look completely like real Japanese anime, as if it were taken directly from a finished theatrical anime film. This is traditional-looking, hand-drawn 2D anime, not a 3D animation, a moving illustration, or a stylized web graphic.

Deliver a single, self-contained HTML file that plays offline, with a synthesized soundtrack. Use any tools, libraries, references, guides, literally anything etc.

Use theatrical samurai and mecha anime as the art style reference for design, line work, painted backgrounds and colour. The film is 84 seconds long, in 40 shots. Its characters are two rival mecha ronin, SUMI and YUKI, and UTSUSHI, a colossal giant made of mirror shards. No people appear in the film. Use any tools or techniques you want, including 3D, as long as the final result looks 100% like hand-drawn 2D anime.

SCENE
Open on an endless mirror lake at sunset: the sky doubled, two tiny silhouettes far apart. Cut between two worlds. In a neon city canyon at night, in the rain, an armoured foot splashes into a puddle full of pink and cyan signs, and SUMI, a heavy black ronin, walks down the street, his red scarf whipping. On a snowy pass at dawn, a white hand brushes snow off a mossy stone lantern, and YUKI, a slim white ronin, walks down stone steps through a broken red gate above a sea of clouds. His red eye slit glows; her cyan eyes breathe vapour. Omens: Sumi's reflection in a puddle turns to the camera with white eyes for three frames while he walks on; a white crack flickers across Yuki's reflection in frozen ice. She leaps off the cliff into the clouds. Match cut on the foot: his foot lands on the mirror lake and one perfect ripple ring crosses the reflected sunset.
They stop sixty metres apart, side on, the sun exactly between them. His thumb pushes the guard, a sliver of steel flashes; she sinks low and draws two blades in reverse grip. Stillness. One leftover raindrop slides off his scarf, hits the lake, and the camera tilts down into the reflection: under their feet the reflected sky holds a colossal face of mirror shards. Its white eyes open. Both look down.
They charge, meet in two impact frames, pass each other and stab their blades into the mirror at the giant's eye. Silence. Cracks race to the horizon and the giant pushes up into the real sky, glass and water pouring off it. Its shard sword carves a wall of spray as they leap over it. Yuki runs up its arm and cracks its face; a red-gold aura ignites along Sumi's blade as his scarf burns into embers. They leap from opposite sides into the sun and cut a giant X through its chest. One second of nothing. The X splits the clouds for kilometres, and the giant bursts into shards that fall like snow. The lake heals. He sheathes with a click; they bow with the sun between them, and walk away in opposite directions, fading to gold.

ANIME QUALITY STANDARD
Every frame must look drawn by professional anime animators and painted by master background artists.
SUMI: 18 m, broad and slow. Low kabuto, a thin gold crescent crest, dark faceplate with one red eye slit FF3B2E, huge lacquered shoulder guards laced with red cord, a tattered red scarf, a long blade with a gold guard. Lacquer 2C3150, gold C9A24A.
YUKI: 15 m, fast and precise. Sleek white helmet with swept blade crests and a long plume, cyan eyes 5CF2FF, slim waist, vermilion edges D2402F, two short blades at her back. White EEEDF2, lavender shade A9ABD0.
UTSUSHI: 200 m, hundreds of irregular mirror shards with thin dark gaps; each shows the sunset sky, sun-facing shards blaze gold, each carries a crisp glint. Its helmet merges both rivals. Eyes like two white suns.
Line art: Confident hand-inked lines with pressure, on every plate boundary.
Coloring: Clean cel areas, hard cool lavender shadows, crisp highlights. Never murky: night is blue-violet, dawn pink-blue, sunset gold and ultramarine.
Backgrounds: Hand-painted gouache: a dense neon street with real kanji signs; a snowy ridge above a sea of clouds; towering sunset cumulus doubled in a perfect mirror.
Lighting: A painted sun, neon glows, and a character key light so faces always read.
Effects: Bold drawn FX on threes: rain, snow, ripple rings, glass, sparks, slashes, speed lines, inverted ink impact frames. Never particle mush.
Animation: Characters on twos, strong key poses, real holds. Huge things move slowly. Nothing clips, slides or floats.
Sound: Original score and effects timed to the picture: a low bamboo flute for Sumi, koto plucks for Yuki, rain, wind, a far temple bell, heartbeat taiko, a single drop ringing, glass tearing, choir and brass over driving taiko, two real silences, a sheathe click, both motifs together at the end.
Direction: Macro close-ups against huge wide shots, stillness before every strike: tense silence, explosive action, quiet respect.

IT MUST NOT LOOK LIKE
- 3D: No plastic materials, CGI shading, visible polygons or game-engine lighting.
- Blocky shapes: No plain boxes or toy proportions. Every plate has seams, bevels or lacing.
- SVG or vector art: No perfect curves, uniform outlines or basic gradients.
- Web animation: No sliding layers, bobbing, software easing or puppet joints.
- Pasted-on elements: No 2D sprites floating in a 3D scene.
- AI art: No warped shapes, melted details, flicker or changing designs.
- Non-anime art: No Western cartoon designs or realistic rendering.
- Amateur work: No stiff poses, empty backgrounds, muddy colors or placeholders.

You are free to change any part of the prompt, if it would result in better results.

It should feel silent, sharp and enormous.

Before finishing, inspect random frames as still images. If any frame does not look completely like real 2D anime, keep improving it.

Do not stop until every frame could pass as a still from a theatrical anime film.

给 bot 派个有明确终点的活跑通，再往上加。 I run a one-person AI media business.
The hardest part isn't making content. It's deciding what to make next week.

Every Monday I used to open 3 dashboards, guess what worked, plan the week in my head, then message my teammate and hope the plan fit their hours.

So I turned my Monday planning into a Loop in @Teamily_AI 2.0: a saved workflow I run every week.

1、A clear process, with fixed roles
Data Agent → Strategy Agent → Planning Agent → Reviewer Agent → my teammate + me.
Agents analyze, plan and check. Humans approve.

2、The Reviewer catches what I'd miss
On the first run, it flagged a post scheduled right in the middle of my shoot, plus a video slot with no production time behind it. It fixed both and rechecked before anything reached me.

3、My teammate has a real say
They said 6 videos was too many for their hours. The Loop didn't start over. Only the planning step re-ran, cut it to 4, and went back to review.

4、One change, the whole week updates
I switched the goal from followers to course sales. The strategy, calendar, task list and final report all rebuilt around it.

5、Next Monday? Just run it again
New numbers in, new plan out. Nothing rebuilt.

Result: what used to eat my whole Monday is now one run of a Loop, checked by an agent and approved by real people.

The actual weekly report the Loop produced is in the comments 👇

组团队、派活那类大家应该刷到很多了，我挑了一部分我日常使用比较多的，直接给 Grok Bot 安装上这 20 个，你的 Grok Bot 可以直接原地起飞 。

🧰 第一组，向外延伸，让它会得更多

1、web-access：给 Grok Bot、Claude Code 这类 Agent 补齐联网能力，会自己开浏览器，还会越用越熟每个网站的门道
https://t.co/QjeH62EOPM

2、grok-bot-clipper：浏览器插件，看到好网页、截图、帖子，一键丢进素材篮发给 bot
https://t.co/fmXXfgJ0Zp

3、cn-mail-mcp：让 bot 读 QQ、163、126 和腾讯企业邮，默认只读，用授权码不用密码
https://t.co/vU2zMtjsqM

4、grokbot-bridge-mcp：在 Cursor、Codex、Claude Code 里一句话给 Grok Bot 派活
https://t.co/SJur2JDOM4

5、grok-bot-cli：终端里建 bot、拉群、发消息、翻聊天记录，适合写脚本批量管
https://t.co/39quuqyHNR

6、grokbot-telegram-bridge：在 Telegram 里跟 bot 聊，桥跑在 bot 自己的云电脑上，带白名单
https://t.co/h95Lg0kIMs

⏳ 第二组长任务和省额度

7、bot-keepalive：云电脑闲 5 分钟左右就会睡，后台任务跟着冻住，这个用一个低档子代理帮你守着
https://t.co/JOeNC2wXfx

8、Wake on Done：活丢给 Codex、Claude Code 跑，跑完自动叫醒 bot 接着干，不用它一直盯着
https://t.co/SB77lUhe66

9、grokbot-local-agent：批量改文件、写长文这种重活，交给云电脑上的 Pi 用你自己的模型账号跑，省 bot 额度
https://t.co/L3F28rSDZS

10、grokbot-usage-cli：让 bot 干活前先看一眼本周额度还剩多少
https://t.co/lsQxboKNTc

📚第三组中文抄作业

11、awesome-grokbot-playbooks：中文配方库，197 个条目逐条核过，还有 10 个拿来就能跑的配方
https://t.co/yJv86w9SuN

12、Grok Bot 橙皮书：1.6 万字，入门到进阶，PDF 免费下。8 月写的，部分细节以官方为准
https://t.co/r4zT3hvOvP

13、grokbot-growth：回答 6 个问题，直接生成一整套出海增长 bot 团队的岗位和开工清单
https://t.co/m5CkW11B6B

14、grok-bot-skills：周报、会议记录转行动卡、公众号小绿书，几个中文 Skill 模板
https://t.co/GcdjqNHDfW

15、grokbot-field-notes：xAI 团队 72 小时直播从零做产品，整理出来的规则和 40 条翻车记录
https://t.co/vALCDmA0Qt

🖥️ 第四组桌面硬件（玩 ESP32 的朋友重点看）

16、宗主：ESP32 圆屏，一对会眨的眼睛，对它说话就能给 Grok Bot 派活
https://t.co/NMit8Pqk50

17、Groki Bot：M5Stack 桌面机器人，喊 Hi Grok 唤醒，还会转头跟着你
https://t.co/D8LJT0beWi

🔓 第五组没有 Grok Bot 也能玩

18、OpenMausBot：开源替代，底层跑你本机的 Claude 或 Codex
https://t.co/pejN5Nl4KY

19、Rakazo：开源自托管，手机电脑都有，模型自己选
https://t.co/jtHq7bdvSb

20、AnyModelBot：跑在自己电脑上，任意模型按量付费
https://t.co/5n4CtXBT4E

⚠️ 这 20 个都是社区项目，不是官方出的，装之前看一眼它要哪些权限，尤其是读邮件、开浏览器这类。

一定要明确自己的使用目的，不能乱装一气。
给 bot 派个有明确终点的活跑通，再往上加。 I run a one-person AI media business.
The hardest part isn't making content. It's deciding what to make next week.

Every Monday I used to open 3 dashboards, guess what worked, plan the week in my head, then message my teammate and hope the plan fit their hours.

So I turned my Monday planning into a Loop in @Teamily_AI 2.0: a saved workflow I run every week.

1、A clear process, with fixed roles
Data Agent → Strategy Agent → Planning Agent → Reviewer Agent → my teammate + me.
Agents analyze, plan and check. Humans approve.

2、The Reviewer catches what I'd miss
On the first run, it flagged a post scheduled right in the middle of my shoot, plus a video slot with no production time behind it. It fixed both and rechecked before anything reached me.

3、My teammate has a real say
They said 6 videos was too many for their hours. The Loop didn't start over. Only the planning step re-ran, cut it to 4, and went back to review.

4、One change, the whole week updates
I switched the goal from followers to course sales. The strategy, calendar, task list and final report all rebuilt around it.

5、Next Monday? Just run it again
New numbers in, new plan out. Nothing rebuilt.

Result: what used to eat my whole Monday is now one run of a Loop, checked by an agent and approved by real people.

The actual weekly report the Loop produced is in the comments 👇
Try Teamily through my invite link: https://t.co/BKFuLw9fxb

Here's the actual weekly report from this Loop, open it and see the plan, the fixes and the approvals: https://t.co/tKZcRO8ME4

The hardest part isn't making content. It's deciding what to make next week.

Every Monday I used to open 3 dashboards, guess what worked, plan the week in my head, then message my teammate and hope the plan fit their hours.

So I turned my Monday planning into a Loop in @Teamily_AI 2.0: a saved workflow I run every week.

Data Agent → Strategy Agent → Planning Agent → Reviewer Agent → my teammate + me.
Agents analyze, plan and check. Humans approve.

2、The Reviewer catches what I'd miss

New numbers in, new plan out. Nothing rebuilt.

第一次真正意义上的做了一个小游戏🎉
以前都是一句提示词出游戏，毫无挑战

这一次把想法跟 Opus5.5 深度沟通叫它帮我出规划
Claude Opus 5.5 + CesiumJS  + GPT Image 2.5 + Tripo + Blender

Opus 规划完毕之后
全程都是让AI 去搭建项目骨架
全程我没有操作 Tripo 和Blender,都交给了 AI。
需要的素材也是让 Opus5.5 把所需提示词写好，然后直接调用 GPT Image 2.5 输出即可

然后游戏中需要的 3D 模型
直接使用 GPT Image 2.5 输出的 2D 图 让 Tripo 进行加工成 3D 的毛坯房
然后再让 Blender 把3D 毛胚房加工成装修房

最开始不懂都是叫AI操作，但是现在懂了，还是想让AI直接去操作。
第一次做成这样的游戏，成就感满满的，但是小游戏需要优化的地方还是蛮多的。

不得不说 Tripo 这个工具实在是太棒了。
并且它还支持 Tripo CLI
同时 Blender 也是支持 CLI的
